revisions.contentCorrection: Clarified post-completion rating submission for both riders and drivers, participant eligibility, idempotency, uniqueness, and durable storage on the existing rider app, driver app, gateway, trip service, and trip store.

assessmentGate.reviewNotes: Run 4 identified concrete clarity gaps in atomic driver reservation, stale-location behavior, fare versioning, and payment recovery. These are being addressed without adding components.

contentCorrections: Atomic trip-version and unique driver-lease transaction with fenced offers
Provisional p95 and location freshness assumptions, fail-closed on lag
Accepted quote ID/version/amount contract with confirmation for repricing
Payment ledger outbox and explicit idempotent outcome path back to trip state
Derived 116 average ride-starts/second baseline for 10M/day; peak factor remains unspecified

Apply monotonic routeVersion/path/ETA updates only to the active trip and propagate them through the existing trip notification/app path
Keep navigation reroutes separate from accepted fare terms; repricing still requires rider confirmation

findings: No explicit active-recipient under-100ms path budget
Partition recovery lacked durable consumer cursor and ownership fencing
Fanout recovery lacked recipient deduplication and ordering-gap behavior
Sender accepted/delivered/read acknowledgement evidence and latency observability needed clearer end-to-end semantics

contentCorrections: Added a provisional active-recipient latency budget and separated durable acceptance from asynchronous delivery
Defined durable consumer checkpoints, replay, and partition-owner fencing
Specified per-recipient deduplication, sequence cursors, and gap recovery using durable history
Made accepted, delivered, and read acknowledgements monotonic and tied each to durable evidence
Added metadata-only trace correlation and provisional end-to-end latency and cursor-stall alerts

browserGate.narrowViewport: 390x844; page width 390px; Previous and Next fully inside viewport

scoredFindings: End-to-end <100ms latency not demonstrated; budgets explicitly provisional
Capacity planning for 50M DAU not quantified
Cost controls for fanout/replay/presence not explained

assessmentGate.reason: Only 2/5 byte-identical runs passed; one validly identified that <100ms was framed as an unproven provisional budget, and two calls returned unavailable rule-based fallbacks.

contentCorrections: Replaced provisional latency language with an explicit active same-region sender-submit to recipient-client-receive p95 <100ms objective, hop ceilings, overload behavior, and direct measurement boundary
Added clearly labeled 50M-DAU traffic assumptions (2.5B writes/day, ~145k peak writes/s, ~435k average fanout deliveries/s, and a 100-member hot-group stress envelope)
Added fanout, presence, receipt-retention, and attachment-CDN cost controls without weakening durable history or delivery semantics
Kept all 16 existing nodes and 21 existing connections; component updates use only catalog-supported purpose properties

browserGate.narrowViewport: 390x844; page width 390px; Next control fully inside viewport

scoredFindings: No explicit cutover/backpressure boundary for hot-group spikes while preserving the online <100ms recipient path
Receipt state and sender-notification delivery lacks a durable, idempotent recovery contract across partial failures

assessmentGate.reason: The browser UI assessment already failed with two scored architecture defects; repeated identical runs were deferred until those real gaps are corrected.

contentCorrections: Defined a bounded online fanout fast lane and offline replay lane; reserve active-recipient capacity before commit and return retryable backpressure before acceptance when the 100ms budget cannot be protected

Made receipt updates idempotent in effect rather than claiming exactly-once transport: atomically persist monotonic state plus sender-notification outbox, replay with stable event_id, dedupe at client, and reconnect from durable state
Added one recovery connection from the existing Conversation Store to existing Delivery Service; no new component types or nodes
Preserved the explicit 50M-DAU capacity/cost assumptions, ordering, fencing, and catalog-supported component properties
